channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: Five reasons no one saw Prince Harry’s return coming
item.dc:creator: Karla Adam
item.description: The decision to trade what appeared to be an idyllic life on the sunny California coast for the Tupperware-gray skies of Britain came as a startling reversal.

item.title: Trump increasingly lashing out at allies as victory in Iran war proves elusive
item.dc:creator: Rachel Chason, Susannah George, Riley Beggin, Mohamad El Chamaa
item.description: Unable to force Tehran’s surrender, President Donald Trump appears to be taking his frustration out on Oman and other U.S. partners in greater measure.

item.title: 7 dead in Kenya helicopter crash in area popular with luxury safari tours
item.dc:creator: Rael Ombuor
item.description: The tourist aircraft crashed into Mount Ololokwe. Among the dead were a Telemundo executive and a Miami restaurateur.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan’s return from California exile sets U.K. aflutter
item.dc:creator: Steve Hendrix, Victoria Craw
item.description: Their move back from the United States sparks questions about security, their formal role — and whether the couple could overshadow the official royal family.

item.title: A royal rift and a surprise return: How the Harry and Meghan saga has unfolded
item.dc:creator: Aoife Walsh, Victoria Craw
item.description: The couple's decision to move back to Britain comes after a high-profile split and tell-all memoir. Here are the biggest moments from a tumultuous eight years.

item.title: Russia bombards Kyiv as fight over elections shatters political unity in Ukraine
item.dc:creator: David Stern, Anastacia Galouchka
item.description: Some political actors are warning that a vote during wartime, which would require changes to Ukraine’s constitution and other laws, could aid Russia by destabilizing the government and dividing society.

item.title: ‘The great Meghan-aissance’: Harry and Meghan’s return sparks frenzied U.K. reaction
item.dc:creator: Victoria Craw
item.description: Where Harry and Meghan will live, why they are returning and what it means for the rest of the royals were among the questions British media outlets are scrambling to answer.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will return to Britain after six years in U.S.
item.dc:creator: Steve Hendrix
item.description: The prince and his wife have been estranged from the royal family but are now returning to England with their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5.

item.title: UAE says it is suspending trade with Iran after missile launch
item.dc:creator: Ellen Francis, Rachel Chason
item.description: The UAE, one of Iran’s biggest trading partners, said the move was “in light of regional escalations that undermine regional and international peace and security.”

item.title: Defense minister dismissed by Zelensky demands elections in Ukraine
item.dc:creator: David Stern, Anastacia Galouchka
item.description: The move from an architect of Ukraine’s drone program is a remarkably direct challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky’s authority and may test Ukrainian unity.
